archetypes.name: artifact-taxonomy
archetypes.rationale: Checks that every planned exclusion glob maps to real producer filenames and sidecars without adding dead or overbroad patterns.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the plan's transcript and sidecar taxonomy matches the actual producer paths and naming conventions in the scoped scripts. Look for missing sidecar families, fictional glob arms, phased-output mismatches, or patterns broad enough to suppress canonical artifacts. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: publication-boundary
archetypes.rationale: Focuses on whether the proposed committed-log boundary is complete, documented, and consistent with security-sensitive artifact handling.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review whether the plan fully preserves the intended boundary between canonical published findings and raw reviewer transcripts or stderr captures. Compare the proposed script, docs, and SECURITY.md changes for omissions or contradictions that could leak raw operational artifacts into committed logs. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: fixture-realism
archetypes.rationale: Targets test-plan holes where fixtures may still use non-production names or fail to prove the intended include/exclude behavior.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether the planned test fixture changes prove behavior for real static, dynamic, phased, and sidecar output names rather than fictional names. Check for assertion gaps, collisions with unrelated JSON or metadata cases, and missing negative coverage for canonical files that must remain published. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
